records.name: OpenAI Codex CLI (codex-rs)
records.version: workspace 0.0.0 at pin (b7ba02f88095, 2026-10-14); latest stable rust-v0.162.1, 0.163.0-alpha.11
records.one_liner: Rust coding-agent product with platform sandboxes and policy controls; a JSON-RPC app-server connects the harness to its hosts, while language SDKs drive subprocesses. The model transport speaks the Responses API.

dims.loop: SQ/EQ: submission_loop dispatches Op; RegularTask→run_turn loops sampling requests, draining steered input and running Stop hooks with continuation. Tool futures start mid-stream (FuturesOrdered). A global RwLock gates non-parallel tools. Retries are unbounded on connection loss, then fall back from WebSocket to HTTPS. Mailbox mail can preempt a response.
dims.providers: Responses API only; wire_api="chat" is a hard error. Built-ins: openai, amazon-bedrock (OpenAI models), ollama, lmstudio, plus custom Responses-compatible providers. store:false with encrypted reasoning replay, WebSocket previous_response_id, prompt_cache_key. Server-driven ModelInfo catalog. Token/rate-limit accounting, no cost.
dims.tools: ToolSpec Function/Freeform-Lark/hosted. Router rebuilt each step with Direct/Deferred(tool_search)/CodeMode exposure. Built-ins: exec_command+write_stdin (PTY), apply_patch grammar, update_plan, view_image, web_search, MCP resources, agent tools, V8 code-mode exec/wait, client dynamic tools. ToolOrchestrator runs approve→sandbox→escalate-on-denial.
dims.context: Base prompt from the model catalog plus 'world state' sections that emit diffs, persisted as RFC 7386 merge patches. AGENTS.override.md/AGENTS.md walked from root to cwd (32 KiB; skipped if untrusted). Compaction: local summary (20k-token user tail), remote V2 compaction_trigger, token-budget reset, async speculative. Two-phase memory pipeline.
dims.state: JSONL rollouts ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD with zstd cold compression; SQLite state DB (61 migrations). Pluggable ThreadStore trait with PersistContext durability barriers. Resume, copied/referenced fork, immutable-file revert, paginated history. Daemon turn suspension and RecoverTurn. No file checkpoints.
dims.safety: AskForApproval (untrusted/on-request/never/granular) × permission profiles. Starlark prefix_rule execpolicy with validated examples; dangerous-command heuristics. Seatbelt sandbox-exec, bwrap+seccomp (vendored bwrap), Windows restricted token/ACL/WFP/MXC. HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy with MITM limited mode. Guardian LLM auto-reviewer; managed requirements. Env inherits all variables by default.
dims.extensibility: 12 Claude-compatible hook events (command/mcp_tool/prompt/agent handlers; Bash/Write/Edit/Agent aliases). SKILL.md skills in .agents/skills. Plugins and marketplaces that also read .claude-plugin/.cursor-plugin. rmcp MCP client (stdio, streamable HTTP, OAuth). Dynamic tools via app-server. Compile-time Rust extension-api for 15 ext crates. 176 feature flags.
dims.multi_agent: V1 (spawn/send_input/resume/wait/close) and V2 (spawn_agent with fork_turns, send_message, followup_task, wait, interrupt, list). Defaults: 6 threads, depth 1. Mailbox with preemption, agent roles, graph store, message board, goal-driven idle continuation. Worktrees only for exec/TUI, not per subagent.
dims.surfaces: TUI and exec are in-process app-server clients (TUI has no codex-core dependency). app-server JSON-RPC over stdio/unix/ws/remote-control: 175 requests, 9 server requests, 86 notifications, exported JSON/TS schema. TS SDK spawns `codex exec --json`; Python SDK spawns app-server. exec-server for remote environments. MCP-server mode removed; no ACP.
dims.observability: OTel logs/traces/metrics (OTLP gRPC/HTTP, Statsig default) with GenAI usage span fields, W3C propagation and opt-in prompt/response logging. rollout-trace bundles via CODEX_ROLLOUT_TRACE_ROOT. `codex debug prompt-input/models`. Analytics and feedback crates. ~1M test LOC but no public eval harness.

builds_on: rmcp (official MCP Rust SDK, git-pinned 3.5.1) for the MCP client
bubblewrap (vendored C source in codex-rs/vendor/bubblewrap) + seccompiler for the Linux sandbox
ratatui for the TUI; sqlx/SQLite for the state DB; portable-pty for unified exec
OpenAI Responses API / ChatGPT Codex backend (chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex) as the only wire protocol
used_by: OpenAI Agents SDK (Python experimental codex extension builds `exec --experimental-json`; JS codexTool() via @openai/codex-sdk)
Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/harness-codex bridges HarnessAgent to the Codex app-server)
Goose (codex provider runs `codex exec --json`; codex-acp provider)
OpenClaw (official extensions/codex app-server plugin and session supervision)
Eve (spawns `codex app-server --stdio`, getAuthStatus, to borrow ChatGPT credentials)
Pi, OpenCode, Kilo, Cline, Mastra Code, Prime Agent reuse ChatGPT/'OpenAI Codex' OAuth and backend, not the harness
Codex VS Code extension and desktop app (closed source, app-server clients)
key_insights: Every first-party surface goes through the JSON-RPC app-server: tui/Cargo.toml has no codex-core dependency and `codex exec` uses InProcessAppServerClient with thread/start + turn/start. The 175-method app-server protocol, not the crate API, is the real embedding contract.

`codex mcp-server` and its crate were deleted in PR #42993 (2026-09-05), which fits OpenAI's account that exposing Codex as an MCP server was abandoned for the app-server. ACP exists only via the third-party codex-acp adapter.

Provider neutrality went down over time: WireApi has one variant, Responses, and `wire_api="chat"` raises a hard error. That unlocks store:false encrypted-reasoning replay, WebSocket incremental requests with previous_response_id, Lark-grammar freeform tools (apply_patch, code-mode exec) and remote compaction V2.

Much harness behavior is server-driven per model through the backend ModelInfo catalog: shell/patch tool type, truncation policy, auto-compact limit (90% default), comp_hash-triggered compaction, tool_mode, prompt and tool description overrides, and Guardian coverage.

Context is a set of typed 'world state' sections that render diffs against a persisted snapshot, stored as RFC 7386 merge patches in the rollout. Environment or permission changes are appended as deltas rather than rewriting the prompt prefix.

Compatibility with Claude Code is visible in code: Claude-named hook events with Bash/Write/Edit/Agent matcher aliases, discovery of .claude-plugin/plugin.json and marketplace.json, and an external-agent-migration crate that imports Claude Code and Cursor config, hooks, subagents and sessions.

Durability is engineered but turn-granular. A ThreadStore trait has explicit PersistContext durability barriers, revert writes a new immutable rollout file plus a SQLite pointer swap, and daemon suspend flushes before cancelling so RecoverTurn can re-run the turn. No tool-level replay or file checkpoints (GhostCommit removed).

Several focus-note assumptions are stale at this pin: there is no core/src/codex.rs (the loop is in session/turn.rs and tasks/), the legacy `shell` tool is replaced by unified exec_command/write_stdin, Linux filesystem isolation is bubblewrap with Landlock only as a rejected legacy path, and docs/protocol_v1.md references a nonexistent Op::ConfigureSession.

features_notes.in_process_sdk: Internal Rust route exists; public TypeScript/Python clients wrap a process.
features_notes.durable_resume: Rollouts and bounded turn recovery do not deduplicate tool effects.
features_notes.worktrees: Git/worktree support in product tooling does not automatically isolate each subagent.
